title: First steps in Advaita
description: Two short works attributed to Śaṅkara, the Gītā's second chapter, three Upaniṣads, and the opening sūtras with Śaṅkara's commentary.

steps.note: A short treatise that, in its opening verses, calls knowledge the only direct means to liberation.
The qualifications for enquiry and the question "Who am I?".
The Way of Knowledge: the Self that is never born and never dies.
Seeing all beings in the Self, and the Self in all beings.
That by which speech and mind are themselves known.
Nachiketas is taught the unborn Self.
The chariot: Self, body, intellect and mind.
The higher and the lower knowledge.
Śaṅkara's introduction on superimposition, and the first sūtra.
Brahman as that from which the world originates.

title: Śaṅkara and Rāmānuja on the first four sūtras
description: Read the two great commentaries side by side where they first diverge.

steps.note: Then therefore the enquiry into Brahman; Rāmānuja's Great Pūrvapakṣa and Siddhānta sit here.
That from which the origin of this world proceeds.
On scripture and the knowledge of Brahman.
Harmony of the Upaniṣads, and whether knowledge is subordinate to action.
